land.text: the South Ossetian Autonomous Oblast around Tskhinvali, within the Georgian SSR

predecessors.note: Georgia abolished the oblast's autonomy on 11 December 1990.

correction.text: the Ossetian-held area around Tskhinvali of the former South Ossetian Autonomous Oblast (3,885 km2 in all)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 1990-2007. Infobox area 3,885 km2 (about 3,900) is the whole oblast; the page gives no pre-2008 line of control. Georgia held Akhalgori, Kurta, Tighva and Eredvi from 2006 (local councils) and set up the Provisional Administrative Entity in April 2007, so a 28 km circle round Tskhinvali (2,530 km2 on the gazetteer, ratio 0.65 to the infobox) stands for the Ossetian-held area; Akhalgori is the eastern part left out.

correction.text: the former autonomous oblast, 'Russian and Ossetian forces gained control of the former autonomous oblast' in August 2008

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 2008-2024: the Tskhinvali circle plus a 20 km circle at Akhalgori (the district Russian and South Ossetian forces took in 2008). The union resolves to 4,046 km2 on the gazetteer (ratio 1.04 to the infobox), though the pieces are circles. Borderisation after 2008 ('nearly 20 militarized border guard bases', 'encroaching occupation') is not drawn.

region.text: the South Ossetian Autonomous Oblast around Tskhinvali

ledger.note: 20 September 1990: the South Ossetian Soviet Democratic Republic is proclaimed. The regional council proclaimed it 'within the Soviet Union on 20 September 1990'; Georgia's government abolished the autonomy on 11 December 1990, calling the Ossetian election illegitimate.

5 January 1991: Georgian troops enter Tskhinvali and the war begins. 'Fighting broke out after Georgian troops entered Tskhinvali on 5 January 1991', with Russia on the Ossetian side; an independence referendum on 19 January 1992 passed but was not recognised.
24 June 1992: the Sochi ceasefire ends the war. Shevardnadze and the South Ossetian government signed the Sochi ceasefire agreement, which 'created a joint peacekeeping force'.

region.text: the Akhalgori district (Kurta, Tighva and Eredvi lie inside the Tskhinvali circle)

ledger.note: August 2008: Russian and Ossetian forces take Akhalgori and the Georgian-held villages. In the August 2008 war 'Russian and Ossetian forces gained control of the former autonomous oblast'; Georgia's local councils at Akhalgori, Kurta, Tighva and Eredvi 'were captured by separatists and Russia in 2008'; Russia recognised South Ossetia on 26 August 2008.

wars.name: South Ossetia War (1991-1992)
wars.outcome: Fighting from Georgia's entry into Tskhinvali (5 January 1991) to the Sochi ceasefire of 24 June 1992, which created a joint peacekeeping force; the republic held the Tskhinvali area.
wars.note: The page also gives the independence referendum of 19 January 1992 and a declaration of independence on 29 May 1992 (infobox: 21 December 1991).

wars.name: Russo-Georgian War (South Ossetian front)
wars.outcome: In August 2008 Russian and Ossetian forces gained control of the former autonomous oblast, including Akhalgori; Russia recognised South Ossetia on 26 August 2008.
wars.note: The dedicated war page was not opened.

certainty.note: The Tskhinvali line of contact before 2008 and the post-2008 administrative boundary line are not given by the page; drawn from circles.

notes: No Cliopatria row. Modern separatist state; Cliopatria's 'Georgia' row (eu-19-b) shows the same ground as Georgian land: the Georgia dossier should record the contest 1991-1992 and the 2008 losses with counterpart republic-of-south-ossetia (and republic-of-abkhazia). The page is inconsistent on the declaration of independence (29 May 1992 in the text, 21 December 1991 in the infobox) and the start of the war (the page says 5 January 1991). Circles stand for the oblast, since the gazetteer has no South Ossetia region: a gap-filler might add 'South Ossetia' and 'Akhalgori' as regions. The Georgian-held pockets before 2008 (Kurta, Tighva, Eredvi) are not drawn separately. Recognition by Russia (26 August 2008) and client status are not drawn: the russian-federation dossier may add vassal_start. wikidata null.
